facts: Choose a side as the base. Its height is measured at a right angle from that base to the opposite corner.
The height may meet the base outside the triangle. Extend the base in a straight line to find it.
Use the height for the chosen base. A slanted side is not that height unless it meets the base at a right angle.
Area is measured in square units: cm$^{2}$, m$^{2}$.
For a cost, find the area, then multiply by the cost per square unit. Buy enough whole rolls or bags to cover all the area.
steps: Identify the base and its perpendicular height (at a right angle to the base or its extension).
Multiply base $\times$ height, then halve the result.
Write the answer with squared units.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The base is $11\text{ cm}$. The height at a right angle to that base is $4\text{ cm}$. The slanted $5\text{ cm}$ side is not needed.
$\text{Area}=11\times4\div2$
$=44\div2$
$=22\text{ cm}^{2}$

Use the actual $9\text{ cm}$ base, not the base together with its extension. The perpendicular height is $6\text{ cm}$ even though it is outside the triangle. The slanted $10\text{ cm}$ side is not needed.
$\text{Area}=9\times6\div2$
$=54\div2$
$=27\text{ cm}^{2}$

Turn one copy around and join it to the other copy. The two equal triangles fill the parallelogram.
$\text{Parallelogram area}=13\times6$
$=78\text{ cm}^{2}$
Each triangle has half that area.
$\text{Triangle area}=78\div2$
$=39\text{ cm}^{2}$
For any triangle, multiply its base by its perpendicular height, then halve the result.

workedExamples.question_text: Triangle A has base $12\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $5\text{ cm}$. Triangle B has base $9\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$. Which has the larger area, and by how many square centimetres?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\text{Area of A}=12\times5\div2$
$=30\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{Area of B}=9\times8\div2$
$=36\text{ cm}^{2}$
$36-30=6$
Triangle B is larger by $6\text{ cm}^{2}$. Compare the areas, not just the base lengths.

workedExamples.question_text: A line from the top corner of a triangle divides its base into $7\text{ m}$ and $11\text{ m}$. Both smaller triangles have perpendicular height $6\text{ m}$. Find their areas and the difference.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\text{First area}=7\times6\div2$
$=21\text{ m}^{2}$
$\text{Second area}=11\times6\div2$
$=33\text{ m}^{2}$
$33-21=12$
The difference is $12\text{ m}^{2}$. Each smaller triangle uses its own base and the common perpendicular height.

workedExamples.question_text: A triangular garden has base $11\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $4\text{ m}$. Soil costs $\$13$ per square metre. Find the cost.
A triangular lawn has base $13\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $6\text{ m}$. Each whole roll of turf covers $8\text{ m}^{2}$. How many rolls must be bought?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\text{Area}=13\times6\div2$
$=78\div2$
$=39\text{ m}^{2}$
$4\times8=32$
Four rolls leave $7\text{ m}^{2}$ uncovered.
$5\times8=40$
Buy $5$ rolls to cover all $39\text{ m}^{2}$.

foundation.solution_text:
The two sides meeting at the right angle give the base and height.
$\text{Area}=9\times6\div2$
$=54\div2$
$=27\text{ cm}^{2}$

The perpendicular height is still $5\text{ cm}$, even though it meets the base line outside the triangle.
$\text{Area}=\text{base}\times\text{height}\div2$
$=14\times5\div2$
$=35\text{ cm}^{2}$

foundation.question_text:
A rectangular block of land measuring $30\text{ m}$ long by $18\text{ m}$ wide is cut in half along a diagonal.
Find the area of each triangular block in $\text{m}^{2}$.
foundation.solution_text:
Each triangle has the same base and height as the rectangle.
$\text{Area}=\text{base}\times\text{height}\div2$
$=30\times18\div2$
$=270\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
Triangle $A$ has a base of $12\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $7\text{ cm}$.
Triangle $B$ has a base of $14\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ cm}$.
Which has the larger area, and by how many $\text{cm}^{2}$?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Area of A}=12\times7\div2$
$=42\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{Area of B}=14\times6\div2$
$=42\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger. Both areas are $42\text{ cm}^{2}$.
$\text{Difference}=42-42=0\text{ cm}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A triangular lawn has a base of $13\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ m}$.
Turf is sold only in whole rolls that each cover $5\text{ m}^{2}$.
How many rolls must be bought?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Area}=13\times6\div2$
$=78\div2$
$=39\text{ m}^{2}$
$7\times5=35$
Seven rolls cover only $35\text{ m}^{2}$, leaving $4\text{ m}^{2}$.
$8\times5=40$
Buy $8$ rolls to cover all $39\text{ m}^{2}$.
